children: Benchmark indices on Wall Street had a mixed session on Wednesday, November 18, as the post-Nvidia earnings optimism fizzled out and traders digested the Fed minutes, Anthropic's IPO pricing, and a meltdown in metal prices globally.

The Dow Jones fell 550 points on Wednesday, taking the three-day loss for the index past 2,100 points. The 30-stock index had declined 750 points on Monday and another 850 points on Tuesday as well. Pressuring the index was UnitedHealth, one of its biggest weightage constituents, which fell 10%, along with shares of Chevron and Caterpillar, which fell between 2% to 4%.
With this fall, the Dow Jones is just 900 points away from a 10% fall from its peak, which would drag the index into a "technical correction."

The S&P 500 ended 0.2% lower, extending its losing streak for the fifth straight session, while both the Nasdaq indices - Composite and 100, gained 0.4% each, putting an end to their recent losing run for now. The losses seen in Nvidia were offset by its peer companies, AMD, Broadcom and Amazon, each of which saw their stock price surge between 4% to 5%, lending support to the tech-heavy index.

Traders also analyzed the Fed minutes, where most officials agreed that more rate hikes are warranted in the future to bring inflation down to their 2% target. Two officials also suggested a 50 basis points rate hike in the December policy if the inflation data turns out to be unfavourable.
Earlier in the day, Fed Governor Christopher Waller hinted at a similar policy stance in an interview to CNBC, suggesting that people will need to be "shocked" if inflation pressures keep persisting.

"I’m very, very concerned about inflation. It’s kind of headed in the wrong direction, and it’s spreading out. If you really want to get it down, you’ve got to start taking more aggressive actions. You might need to like, shock people."

Metals continued to sell-off in the global markets overnight, with Gold prices falling another 3.5% to their lowest level since September 2025, while Silver prices fell over 5%. Silver prices had made a record high of over $120 earlier this year, but have now corrected to less than $45 an ounce. The sell-off in Copper prices also continued with the metal falling to the lowest level since April on the London Metals Exchange (LME).
An aggressive policy posture from the Fed, which in-turn strengthened the US Dollar, is adding to the pressure on Metal prices. The US Dollar Index is now nearing levels of 104.
AI Lab Anthropic will be making its Wall Street debut later this evening in what promises to be the world's biggest IPO in history, surpassing the SpaceX issue just a few months earlier.

The company has priced its IPO at $83 per share, which is above the earlier marketed range of $70 to $78 apiece. The IPO size has also been upsized, with the company selling 980 million shares instead of the 825 million shares planned earlier. This, along with the pre-committed investment of $26 billion, the total fund raise would cross $100 billion.
Both Amazon and Google, which own significant stakes in the company, are likely to see their holdings be valued at over $100 billion each.

title: Dow Jones falls another 550 points, nears 'technical correction' - Here's what transpired
